data.name: Gas Prices and Iran War Dominate Voter Concerns Before Midterms
data.summary: High gas prices, fueled by the war in Iran that started with U.S. and Israeli strikes in February, top conservatives' worries as voters head to the polls Tuesday. Everyday people focus on pocketbook issues like $5.93 average regular gas in California—far above the national $4.22 to $4.31—rather than online debates over podcasters. While some blame influencers for Republicans' polling struggles, others like Megan Basham and Auron MacIntyre stress that face-to-face talks reveal inflation, fuel costs, and the war as the real voter priorities ahead of deciding Congress control.

data.name: Cook Report Shifts 12 House Races to Democrats Ahead of Midterms

data.hook: House Speaker Mike Johnson touted Republican gains on borders and crime, only to face quick pushback highlighting a record homicide spike under Trump in 2020.
data.name: Political Clash Over Crime Rates, Borders, and Inflation Trends
data.summary: Johnson posted that Democratic policies led to high inflation, millions of border entries, and crime, while Republicans delivered 3.4% inflation, zero interior releases in fiscal 2026, and a murder rate at a 120-year low of about 4.1 per 100,000. Critics countered with data showing a 30% homicide jump from 2019 to 2020—the largest in modern history—amid the pandemic and unrest during Trump's term. The back-and-forth underscores how both sides spotlight favorable stats on crime declines since 2020, border drops from over 2 million encounters to historic lows, and inflation's fall from 9.1%, as midterms near.
